items.headline: Victoria's cross-border transmission line is already under contract, turning an election promise to scrap it into a termination-liability question
items.summary: Reporting on Victoria's November election set out that the state government has already signed a build contract with Iberdrola for the 240 km VNI West line into NSW, and that cancelling it — as the Coalition has pledged, alongside a pause and review of the Western Renewables Link — could expose Victorian taxpayers to liability payments. The same piece notes the state auditor-general's finding that the project is two years behind schedule and will not be finished until 2030, two years after the Yallourn coal plant closes.
items.so_what: The relevant read-across for EnergyCo is not the Victorian politics but the precedent: a transmission project can reach a signed network-operator contract and still face cancellation at an election, with the cost landing on the state. With the NSW Coalition already committed to scaling back regional REZs, EnergyCo's counterparty arrangements with ACEREZ and Transgrid carry the same structural exposure, and the Yallourn timing gap is a reminder that a slipped transmission date against a fixed coal-closure date is the reliability risk that gets attributed to the delivery agency.
